68f844b01c69.title: Plan phase: Greenfield Architecture & Local Foundation Design

T-001.title: Audit & Validate Project Context and Roadmap Documents
T-001.description: Read and validate PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md to extract governing constraints, technology stack decisions, target environment (local-first), scope boundaries, and phase-0 deliverables. Identify any ambiguities or missing information that require research resolution before architecture begins. Produce a structured summary document capturing: tech stack, non-negotiables, out-of-scope items (e.g., advanced custom charting), and open questions.
acceptance_criteria: All fields in PROJECT_CONTEXT.md are parsed and documented in a structured summary
All phase-0 deliverables from ROADMAP.md are itemized with clear done-criteria
Scope boundaries explicitly documented: what is IN scope for phase 0, what is explicitly FUTURE
Open questions list produced with ≥1 entry if any ambiguity exists
No undocumented assumptions remain after review

review_findings.title: Source files PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md never read — audit is based entirely on assumptions
review_findings.description: The task explicitly requires reading and validating PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md. The agent acknowledged these files do not exist on disk (OQ-001, flagged as BLOCKER). However, the agent then proceeded to produce a 'COMPLETE' status document and marked D1 as 'IN PROGRESS' rather than 'BLOCKED'. The acceptance criteria state 'All fields in PROJECT_CONTEXT.md are parsed and documented' and 'All phase-0 deliverables from ROADMAP.md are itemized with clear done-criteria' — neither criterion is satisfied because the source files were never read. All tech stack, non-negotiables, scope boundaries, and phase-0 deliverables documented in context_audit_summary.md are self-derived from the task prompt, not from the governing documents. The document header says 'Status: COMPLETE' which is factually incorrect.
review_findings.recommendation: This deliverable CANNOT be marked complete or even 'IN PROGRESS' until PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md are provided and actually parsed. The summary document status must be changed to 'BLOCKED'. The agent must not proceed to generate downstream artifacts (D2–D7) until OQ-001 is resolved by the user/project manager. Gate condition 5 ('No BLOCKER findings outstanding') already prevents phase-1 progression, but the D1 status field must also be corrected.

review_findings.title: Document header timestamp '2025-01-01' contradicts agent metadata timestamp '2026-07-25'
review_findings.description: context_audit_summary.md and open_questions.md both carry '**Date:** 2025-01-01'. The agent metadata field '_meta.timestamp' is '2026-07-25T13:15:47.204993+00:00'. One of these is fabricated or incorrect. A 1.5-year discrepancy is not a timezone issue. Stale or fabricated timestamps undermine audit provenance and traceability.
review_findings.recommendation: Set the document date to the actual generation date (matching _meta.timestamp or wall-clock time at artifact creation). Do not hardcode arbitrary past dates in audit documents. Consider auto-inserting the current UTC date via a script or template to prevent recurrence.

review_findings.title: Tests validate documents written by the same agent — circular self-validation with no independent grounding
review_findings.description: The tests in test_audit_documents.py check that the audit documents contain specific strings (e.g., 'Technology Stack', 'Non-Negotiables', 'OQ-'). These documents were authored by the same agent in the same task run. The tests trivially pass because the agent wrote both the documents and the tests to match each other. There is no independent ground truth being verified. For example, test_missing_source_files_flagged passes because the agent wrote 'PROJECT_CONTEXT' in the open_questions.md it also authored. The test suite provides zero assurance that the documents are actually correct or complete relative to the real PROJECT_CONTEXT.md/ROADMAP.md.
review_findings.recommendation: Tests should verify documents against the actual source files once they exist (e.g., parse PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and assert each field appears in the summary). Until the source files exist, tests should assert BLOCKED/PENDING status rather than structural completeness. Add a test that fails if PROJECT_CONTEXT.md is missing (forcing the gate to block rather than pass).

review_findings.title: All 20 test results reported as PASSED are unverifiable — no independent execution evidence
review_findings.description: The agent reports 'tests_passed: true' and lists 20 tests all with status 'PASSED'. However, there is no CI log, no pytest output artifact, no stdout capture, and no independent execution of the test suite. The test results are self-reported by the implementing agent. The phase specification requires independent review; self-reported pass/fail does not satisfy that requirement. Per evidence integrity standards, these are estimates/claims, not measured results.
review_findings.recommendation: Require test execution to produce an independent artifact (e.g., pytest --tb=short --junitxml=test-results.xml) that is committed alongside the code. The reviewer or CI system must execute the tests independently and compare results. Until independent execution is confirmed, all test statuses must be treated as unverified claims.

review_findings.title: context_audit_summary.md Section 6 documents 'expected' fields rather than actual parsed fields
review_findings.description: Section 6 ('Parsed PROJECT_CONTEXT.md Fields') contains a disclaimer: 'If PROJECT_CONTEXT.md does not yet exist on disk, the fields below represent the expected structure'. All fields show 'PENDING' validation status. The section heading says 'Parsed' but nothing was actually parsed. This is misleading — the section title implies parsing occurred when it did not. Similarly Section 7 for ROADMAP.md.
review_findings.recommendation: Rename Section 6 to 'Expected PROJECT_CONTEXT.md Structure (NOT YET PARSED — See OQ-001)' and Section 7 equivalently. Make the BLOCKED status prominent at the top of both sections, not buried in a note. This prevents downstream agents from misreading 'PENDING' as 'partially done' rather than 'completely unstarted'.

review_findings.title: Tech stack in summary is derived from phase specification prompt, not from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md — undocumented assumption
review_findings.description: The acceptance criteria state 'No undocumented assumptions remain after review.' The tech stack table (Python 3.11+, SQLite, FastAPI, pytest) was synthesized from the phase specification text, not read from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md. The document does not explicitly state this provenance. A reader could incorrectly infer these values were extracted from the governing documents. This violates the no-undocumented-assumptions criterion.
review_findings.recommendation: Add an explicit provenance note to the tech stack table and all sections derived from the phase specification rather than from the source files: 'SOURCE: Derived from Phase Specification prompt — NOT from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md (file missing, see OQ-001). Must be re-verified once governing documents are available.'

review_findings.title: No test verifies that PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md are absent — tests should fail (or warn) when source files are missing
review_findings.description: The test suite passes entirely even though the primary inputs for the audit task (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, ROADMAP.md) are missing. There is no test that asserts these files exist or that explicitly marks the test run as incomplete when they are absent. A green test suite implies the task is complete, which is misleading given OQ-001 is a BLOCKER.
review_findings.recommendation: Add a test (or test fixture) that checks for the existence of PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md and marks the test run as XFAIL or raises a clearly labeled skip/warning: 'BLOCKER: Source documents missing — audit incomplete'. This ensures no CI pipeline can report a clean green build while the governing documents are absent.

review_findings.title: D1 done-criterion 'No undocumented assumptions remain' marked unchecked but no resolution path defined
review_findings.description: The checklist marks '[ ] No undocumented assumptions remain' as unchecked (blocked). However, the document does not specify what constitutes 'no undocumented assumptions' or how this will be verified once OQ-001 is resolved. Without a concrete verification method, this criterion risks being checked off without genuine validation.
review_findings.recommendation: Add a concrete verification method to this criterion: 'Verified by: Cross-referencing each entry in context_audit_summary.md against PROJECT_CONTEXT.md verbatim fields. Reviewer attests no fields were inferred beyond documented file contents.' This prevents premature sign-off.

review_findings.title: Data ingestion pipeline listed as IN SCOPE for Phase 0 — may be premature without source document confirmation
review_findings.description: Section 3 lists 'Data ingestion pipeline (local file / mock data sources)' as IN SCOPE for Phase 0. This was inferred from the phase specification, not confirmed from ROADMAP.md. If ROADMAP.md scopes Phase 0 differently, this could represent silent scope expansion — exactly what the non-negotiables prohibit.
review_findings.recommendation: Flag this item as 'ASSUMED from phase spec — must be confirmed from ROADMAP.md (OQ-001)' in the scope boundaries section. Do not begin any ingestion pipeline implementation until ROADMAP.md is available and confirms this scope item.

review_findings.title: OQ-002 through OQ-005 are valid but should be marked as lower priority than OQ-001
review_findings.description: OQ-002 (Python version), OQ-003 (frontend tech), OQ-004 (data source format), OQ-005 (review process) are all legitimately open questions. However, they are secondary to OQ-001 — resolving them before OQ-001 could lead to wasted effort if PROJECT_CONTEXT.md contradicts the assumed answers. The questions are listed without explicit priority ordering.
review_findings.recommendation: Add a priority field or explicit note to OQ-002 through OQ-005: 'Blocked on OQ-001 — do not attempt resolution until PROJECT_CONTEXT.md is available, as that document may already answer this question.' This prevents parallel work on lower-priority questions that may be invalidated.

review_findings.title: pytest import listed but not verified as importable in the test file
review_findings.description: test_audit_documents.py imports pytest but does not use any pytest-specific features (fixtures, marks, parametrize). The import is unused beyond the implicit test collection. More critically, there is no pytest.ini, pyproject.toml [tool.pytest], or conftest.py referenced or created in this task, meaning the test suite has no verified configuration.
review_findings.recommendation: Remove the unused 'import pytest' or use it (e.g., pytest.mark.xfail for the missing-source-files scenario per F-007). Ensure a minimal pytest configuration exists (even a one-line pyproject.toml section) so tests are reproducibly runnable by anyone following the README.

T-002.title: Research: Local-First Technology Stack Validation
T-002.description: Research and validate the specific versions, compatibility matrix, and known issues for all phase-0 candidate technologies: local database engine (e.g., SQLite/DuckDB/PGlite), backend framework, frontend framework, local state management, build tooling, and dev environment toolchain. Produce a compatibility matrix and a recommended pinned dependency list. Verify that chosen stack supports offline-first/local operation, is actively maintained, and has no blocking license conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix produced covering all major dependencies and their interactions
Pinned versions list produced for all core dependencies
License compatibility confirmed for all dependencies (no GPL conflicts if proprietary build intended)
No known critical CVEs in pinned versions (checked against OSV/npm audit/pip audit)
Local-first capability confirmed: app can run fully offline with chosen stack
Decision rationale documented for each major technology choice

T-003.title: Design Overall System Architecture
T-003.description: Design the high-level greenfield architecture for the local-first application. Define the layered architecture (e.g., presentation, application/service, domain, persistence layers), module boundaries, data flow diagrams, and component interaction contracts. Specify the local storage strategy (file layout, database file location, migration ownership). Define the IPC or API boundary if a backend process is separate from the frontend. Produce Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for each significant design choice. Explicitly mark any future-phase concerns (e.g., advanced charting) as out-of-scope with placeholders only.
acceptance_criteria: System architecture diagram produced (C4 or equivalent, at least context and container levels)
Layer definitions and responsibilities documented with no overlapping ownership
Data flow diagram covers all primary user-facing flows planned for phase 0
ADR produced for each major decision (≥3 ADRs expected: DB engine, frontend framework, local storage layout)
Out-of-scope future concerns are explicitly listed with placeholder stubs only—no implementation
Architecture reviewed against PROJECT_CONTEXT.md constraints with zero violations found

T-004.title: Design Local Database Schema (Initial)
T-004.description: Design the initial database schema for the local store based on the domain model derived from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md. Define all entities, relationships, primary keys, foreign keys, indexes, and constraints needed for phase-0 functionality. Produce an entity-relationship diagram (ERD). Define the migration strategy (tool selection, file naming convention, rollback policy). Write the initial schema migration file (migration 0001). Ensure schema supports local file-based operation (no server required). Document data types with explicit handling for edge cases (nullability, text encoding, date storage format).
acceptance_criteria: ERD produced covering all phase-0 entities with cardinalities labeled
All tables have explicit primary keys; no implicit rowid-only tables
Foreign key constraints defined for all relationships
At least one index defined per frequently-queried foreign key column
Migration tool selected and documented (e.g., Flyway, Alembic, golang-migrate, Drizzle)
Migration file 0001_initial_schema.sql (or equivalent) created and applies cleanly from empty DB
Rollback/down migration defined for migration 0001
Schema review confirms no phase-0 features are impossible to implement with this schema

T-005.title: Scaffold Project Repository Structure
T-005.description: Create the canonical directory structure for the project repository according to the architecture designed in T-003. This includes: root config files (linter, formatter, gitignore, editorconfig), source directories for each architectural layer, test directories mirroring source layout, docs directory structure, CI configuration skeleton, and a working build script. Initialize the chosen package manager lockfile. Ensure the scaffold builds and passes an empty test suite from a clean checkout. Document the project structure in a CONTRIBUTING.md or PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md file.
acceptance_criteria: Repository structure matches architecture diagram from T-003 with 1:1 correspondence
Clean checkout + install + build completes in under 3 minutes on a modern developer machine
Empty test suite runs and passes (zero tests, zero failures)
Linter and formatter configs present and enforce on CI (pre-commit or CI step)
.gitignore covers all build artifacts, local DB files, secrets, and IDE configs
CONTRIBUTING.md or PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md explains every top-level directory
No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or environment-specific absolute paths present in committed files

T-006.title: Implement Local Development Environment Setup & Dev Toolchain
T-006.description: Implement the local developer setup experience: environment variable management (e.g., .env.example with all required vars documented, no defaults for secrets), local DB initialization script (creates and seeds dev DB from migration 0001), hot-reload dev server configuration, and a Makefile or task runner (e.g., Taskfile.yml) with canonical commands (dev, build, test, lint, migrate, seed, clean). Verify the setup works from a clean state with a documented one-command bootstrap. Write a DEVELOPMENT.md guide covering all prerequisites and bootstrap steps.
acceptance_criteria: .env.example committed with all required environment variables documented and no secret values
make dev (or equivalent) starts local dev environment with hot reload in under 30 seconds
make test runs full test suite against local dev DB
make migrate applies all pending migrations to local DB idempotently
make seed populates local DB with deterministic dev seed data
make clean removes all build artifacts and local DB, leaving a pristine state
DEVELOPMENT.md documents all prerequisites (Node version, Python version, etc.) with exact version pins
A developer following DEVELOPMENT.md from scratch on a vanilla OS reaches running dev server in under 15 minutes

T-007.title: Implement Core Logging, Error Handling & Observability Foundation
T-007.description: Implement the foundational cross-cutting concerns for a local-first app: structured logging (writing to local log file and optionally console), a global error boundary/handler pattern, and a telemetry/metrics stub (local-only, no external calls) that can be activated for debugging. Define log levels, log file rotation policy, and error categorization (recoverable vs. unrecoverable). Ensure no PII is logged by default. The implementation must be wired into the application entry point and tested.
acceptance_criteria: Structured logger implemented with at least 4 levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
All log output includes timestamp, level, module, and correlation ID
Log output writes to a configurable local file path (not hardcoded)
Log rotation configured: max file size and max retained files defined
Global error handler implemented: unhandled exceptions are caught, logged, and application exits gracefully with non-zero code
No PII fields (email, name, passwords) appear in any log output at INFO or above
Telemetry stub present but disabled by default; enable via env var only
Logger and error handler are unit tested with ≥90% branch coverage

T-008.title: Implement Configuration Management System
T-008.description: Implement a type-safe, validated configuration system that loads settings from: (1) default values, (2) config file (local, user-editable), (3) environment variables (override). Define all phase-0 configuration keys with types, defaults, validation rules, and documentation. Configuration must be validated at application startup with clear error messages for invalid values. Sensitive config values must never be logged. Provide a config schema document.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration loader implemented supporting three-tier precedence: defaults < config file < env vars
All config keys for phase 0 defined in a single schema with types, defaults, and descriptions
Startup validation rejects invalid config values with human-readable error message before app runs
Sensitive keys (passwords, tokens) are masked in all log/debug output
Config schema document committed to docs/
Configuration module has ≥85% line coverage in unit tests
Config file format is human-editable (TOML or YAML preferred over binary formats)

T-009.title: Implement Application Entry Point & Startup/Shutdown Lifecycle
T-009.description: Implement the application entry point that wires together: config loading (T-008), logging init (T-007), database connection/migration check (T-004/T-006), and graceful shutdown handling (SIGTERM/SIGINT or platform equivalent). The startup sequence must be deterministic and ordered. Startup failures must produce actionable error messages. Graceful shutdown must close DB connections and flush log buffers before exit.
acceptance_criteria: Application starts successfully from make dev and make build outputs
Startup sequence is logged with timestamps for each stage (config, logging, DB, server)
If DB migration is behind, startup either auto-migrates or halts with clear instructions
SIGTERM/SIGINT triggers graceful shutdown: DB connections closed, log buffers flushed, exit code 0
Unrecoverable startup error (e.g., DB file locked) produces actionable error message and exit code non-zero
End-to-end startup time on local machine documented and under 5 seconds for dev mode
Integration test verifies full startup → shutdown cycle without errors

T-010.title: CI Pipeline Foundation
T-010.description: Implement a minimal but complete CI pipeline (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or equivalent as specified in PROJECT_CONTEXT.md) that runs on every pull request and main branch push. Pipeline must include: dependency install, build, lint, unit tests, integration tests, security scan (secret detection + dependency vulnerability audit), and produce artifacts (test coverage report, build output). Pipeline must be fast enough to not block developer flow (target: under 10 minutes for full run).
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline triggers on PR open/update and push to main branch
Pipeline stages: install, lint, build, unit-test, integration-test, security-scan
All prior tasks' tests (T-004 through T-009) run in CI and must pass for pipeline to pass
Coverage report artifact generated and published (HTML + summary in PR comment if supported)
Secret scan (gitleaks or equivalent) runs and fails pipeline on any finding
Dependency vulnerability audit runs and fails pipeline on critical CVE findings
Full pipeline completes in under 10 minutes on standard CI runner
Pipeline configuration committed to repo (.github/workflows/ or equivalent)

T-011.title: Phase 0 Architecture Review & Documentation Finalization
T-011.description: Conduct a structured independent review of all phase-0 deliverables before gate closure. Reviewer checks: architecture completeness against ROADMAP.md phase-0 requirements, test coverage targets met, no scope creep (grep for future-phase implementations), all ADRs present, CI passing, DEVELOPMENT.md accurate, all evidence artifacts committed. Produce a phase-0 gate review report. Remediate any BLOCKER or HIGH findings. Record lessons learned in KnowledgeLearning log.
acceptance_criteria: All T-001 through T-010 acceptance criteria confirmed met by independent reviewer
Zero BLOCKER findings remain open at gate closure
Zero HIGH findings remain open at gate closure (or have accepted risk with owner assigned)
Scope compliance confirmed: grep for future-scope keywords (charting, advanced, FUTURE) returns only placeholder comments
All 8 standard gate checklist items verified (from phase spec)
Phase-0 gate review report committed to docs/phase0-gate-review.md
Lessons learned committed to docs/knowledge-log.md
Manager state update confirms phase 0 complete before phase 1 begins
